messages.content:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: To carry out repairs, the Landlord may enter the unit on 24 hours' written notice stating the reason and the day, at any time between 7 a.m. and 10 p.m.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
The clause is not enforceable. Section 26 of the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* allows a landlord to enter a rental unit to carry out repairs only on at least 24 hours' written notice, and only between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. unless the tenant consents to another time. The clause permits entry from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., so it allows entry outside the statutory window without consent.

Under section 3, the Act prevails over a conflicting lease term. Under section 4, a tenant cannot waive or agree to give up the Act's protections, so the clause is void to the extent it exceeds the 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. limit. The 24-hour notice requirement is consistent with the Act, but the hours are not. The rest of the clause would stand, with entry limited to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. (or other times the tenant agrees to).

I have quoted section 26 from memory, so please check the current wording on e-Laws (ontario.ca/laws) before relying on it.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 26
